edges.description: Inner-ear sensory neurons are completely absent and no afferent fibre reaches the ear, which is the mouse counterpart of the imaged eighth-nerve agenesis in patients.
edges.limitations: The mouse lesion is complete absence, whereas human imaging describes a range from agenesis to severe hypoplasia or truncation, so the human deficit is at least sometimes partial. The mouse null also dies within about 12 hours of birth, so the model cannot report the natural history that patients live through.

nodes.description:
Neurogenin 1 is expressed by placodal ectodermal cells and acts before neuroblast delamination, switching on a cascade of downstream bHLH factors (NeuroD, MATH3, NSCL1) that carries the commitment forward. The step it controls is determination, not migration or axon guidance, which is what separates this disorder from the CCDDs caused by axon-pathfinding genes.
The division of labour between the two neurogenins is what makes the phenotype selective: NEUROG1 specifies the proximal ganglia, which arise from the trigeminal and otic placodes and the neural crest, while NEUROG2 specifies the distal, epibranchial-placode-derived ganglia. Only the proximal set is lost.

nodes.description: The cornea loses both its sensory supply and the trophic support that supply provides. Corneal nerves do two things: they carry sensation, and they release neuropeptides that keep the epithelium metabolically and mitotically active. Losing them therefore costs both the reflex and the tissue, which is why this node branches to an absent reflex on one side and to epithelial breakdown on the other.

meta.association: NEUROG1 (5q31.1) encodes neurogenin 1, a proneural class II basic helix-loop-helix transcription factor. It is a single-exon gene encoding a 237-residue protein whose bHLH domain spans residues 92-144. It is the only gene associated with this disorder, and the disorder is the only human phenotype associated with the gene.

nodes.description: Biallelic NEUROG1 variants abolish or degrade the transcriptional activity of neurogenin 1. The four reported alleles are a whole-gene deletion, a nonsense allele, a frameshift allele and a missense substitution, and they converge on the same target: all disrupt the bHLH domain, which carries both the basic region that binds the E-box and the helix-loop-helix region that mediates dimerization. A whole-gene deletion and a point lesion producing the same disorder is what identifies the mechanism as loss of function.

nodes.description:
Loss of the trigeminal sensory neurons, removing the afferent limb of the fifth cranial nerve.
In humans this node is inferred functionally rather than demonstrated anatomically in most patients. Corneal anaesthesia with an absent corneal reflex is present across the reported series, and oromotor dysfunction is too, but a structural abnormality of the fifth nerve has been described in only one reported patient, and the authors of the fourth report state explicitly that their two patients had no fifth-nerve abnormality on imaging. The functional deficit and the imaging finding therefore do not track each other, and this entry records the functional claim.

This is the most consistently demonstrated lesion in the disorder: it has been imaged in every reported family, as agenesis, truncation, or severe hypoplasia. In the mouse null no afferent, efferent or autonomic fibre reaches the ear at all, and the efferent and autonomic losses are secondary to the missing afferents.
